$schema_note: Reusable kernel-family catalog for Hygon HCU/HIP optimization. It guides agent reasoning and automatic handoff decisions; it is not a substitute for correctness, benchmark, hipprof, and dccobjdump gates.

attention.scope: QK/AV attention kernels, causal or padding masks, relative/position bias, scale, activation, dropout-free inference paths, and fused attention epilogues.
profiler_symptoms: kernels or op names contain attention, qk, qkv, av, causal, mask, bias, score, softmax, paged, flash
hipMemcpy or layout kernels surround QK/AV and indicate padding/transposition overhead
softmax, bias, mask, and activation are separate kernels around matmul-like work
low CU activity on skinny decode or current-token eval path
high LDS, waitcnt, or barrier stall around tiled score/value loops
semantic_traps: Causal mask direction and inclusive/exclusive diagonal must match reference exactly.
Relative bias bucketization can be a separate semantic op; do not fold it unless bucket contract is captured.
Forward-only eval fast paths must not be used for training when backward semantics differ.
Softmax numerical stability requires max subtraction and explicit tolerance policy.
Dropout, RNG, and deterministic training paths require separate handling.
Jagged or padded attention must preserve invalid-token zeroing and length semantics.
branch_generator_plan: split QK, softmax, and AV attribution before replacing the whole attention block
try fusion of bias/mask/scale/activation when parity is simple and tensors are contiguous
try head-major or contiguous layout variants only when layout conversion cost is included in e2e benchmark
try decode/current-token specialized path separately from full-sequence training
prefer CK Tile or source-backed HCU examples for matrix-core QK/AV work
correctness_gates: operator parity on tiny shapes with unique q/k/v/bias values
real shape parity with max_abs and max_rel error
mask edge cases: empty, first token, last token, full length, ragged length
training backward parity if optimization is enabled with gradients
fallback path test for unsupported dtype/layout/mask
stop_reasons: profile shows attention share below target threshold after accepted changes
QK/AV already uses proven MMAC/CK Tile path and remaining time is memory movement outside kernel
semantic contract is incomplete for mask/bias/dropout/backward
candidate branch improves microbench but fails e2e or accuracy gate
layout conversion cost cancels kernel-only speedup
library_references: Composable Kernel / CK Tile attention and GEMM examples

gather_scatter_index_add_embedding_backw.scope: Irregular indexed reads/writes, embedding forward/backward, index_add/scatter_add, histogram/bincount-style gradient reduction, and duplicate-index accumulation.
profiler_symptoms: kernels or ops contain index_select, index_add, scatter, gather, embedding, bincount, atomic
global memory request pressure is high while arithmetic intensity is low
atomic pressure or serialization dominates duplicate-index backward
profile attribution points to PyTorch index_select_backward or embedding backward
small output domain with large repeated input ids indicates reduce-by-key opportunity
required_contract_fields: known small output domain if any
semantic_traps: Duplicate indices require accumulation for index_add/scatter_add/embedding backward; plain scatter is not equivalent.
Atomic accumulation changes floating-point order and may need tolerance or deterministic fallback.
Out-of-bound, negative, padding_idx, and ignore-index semantics must match framework behavior.
In-place alias between input/output/index must be captured before replacing a framework op.
Small-domain reduction can beat atomics, but only when bucket/domain size is known and stable.
branch_generator_plan: coarsened flat-index gather/scatter baseline
duplicate-aware atomic branch for general index_add
small-domain bucket-reduction branch for histogram or embedding-gradient style updates
sorted-index segmented reduction branch when sorted or sortable ids are available
two-phase local accumulation plus global atomic branch when duplicate rate is high
correctness_gates: boundary indices: 0 and last valid id
comparison against framework op for forward and backward
repeat-run nondeterminism tolerance check when atomics are used
stop_reasons: duplicate rate is low and memory coalescing branch already saturates bandwidth
duplicate rate is high but output domain is too large for local reduction
deterministic accumulation is required and atomic branch cannot satisfy tolerance
index bounds or alias semantics cannot be proven
framework-level rewrite removes hotspot without custom kernel
library_references: FBGEMM GPU jagged and embedding operators

jagged_ragged_sparse.scope: Variable-length tensor kernels, lengths/offsets based layouts, CSR-like sparse rows, jagged-to-dense or dense-to-jagged transforms, and ragged attention/reduction paths.
profiler_symptoms: ops or kernels contain jagged, ragged, lengths, offsets, csr, segment, pack, pad, dense_to_jagged, jagged_to_dense
many tiny kernels around padding, masking, or copy transforms
hipMemcpy or memset appears between jagged layout conversion steps
low CU activity from short rows or imbalanced segment lengths
scatter/gather kernels dominate around sequence packing
semantic_traps: Offsets must be monotonic and final offset must equal nnz.
Empty segments and max-length truncation are common correctness failures.
Padding value and invalid-token zeroing must match the model path.
Dense conversion may appear faster in microbench but regress memory footprint or e2e.
Load balance across rows matters more than flat element count for ragged kernels.
branch_generator_plan: one-row-per-block branch for medium rows
one-wave-per-row branch for short rows on wave64
persistent work-queue branch for highly imbalanced row lengths
fuse jagged layout conversion with consumer when the consumer is single-use
specialize max_length buckets when dynamic shape distribution is stable
correctness_gates: all rows same length as dense-equivalent control
offset monotonicity and final nnz assertions
stop_reasons: profile shows conversion kernels, not jagged compute, are the true bottleneck
row-length distribution is too dynamic for a single specialized kernel
padding/layout transform cost exceeds fused-kernel gain
contract capture cannot prove offsets/lengths semantics
load imbalance remains but persistent scheduler overhead cancels benefit

segmented_reduction.scope: Reductions over variable-size groups or keys, including reduce-by-key, histogram/bincount, grouped sums, and gradient accumulation by bucket.
profiler_symptoms: ops or kernels contain segment, reduce_by_key, bincount, histogram, bucket, group_reduce
index_add/scatter_add hotspot has high duplicate rate
atomicAdd dominates and output domain is much smaller than input size
separate sort/unique/reduce stages appear around sparse gradients
barrier or LDS pressure appears in custom row/group reductions
required_contract_fields: segment ids or offsets shape and dtype
number of segments or output domain
semantic_traps: Unsorted key reduction and offset-based segmented reduction are different contracts.
Floating accumulation order can change numerical results.
Empty segment initial values must match reference.
Atomic and two-phase reductions need explicit output initialization semantics.
Segment id bounds must be validated or safely guarded.
branch_generator_plan: small-domain histogram branch with per-block partials
offset-based one-block-per-segment branch
wave-level short-segment branch
two-phase partial reduction plus final combine
reduce-by-key branch only when sorted keys or sorting cost is included
stop_reasons: keys are unsorted and sort cost exceeds reduction gain
duplicate distribution does not justify local accumulation
output domain too large for practical per-block partials
deterministic result is required but branch relies on unordered atomics
library primitive is available and faster than custom branch
library_references: rocPRIM reduce_by_key, segmented_reduce, scan, histogram primitives

custom_autograd_backward.scope: Model-local custom backward kernels replacing expensive generic autograd paths such as index_select_backward, index_add accumulation, gather/scatter backward, normalization backward, or fused forward recomputation.
profiler_symptoms: torch or framework attribution points to backward/autograd node rather than forward kernel
kernel names contain backward, grad, index_select_backward, embedding_backward, index_add
forward is cheap but backward launches multiple gather/scatter/reduction kernels
autograd saves large tensors or performs extra copies/syncs
manual PyTorch primitive rewrite improves semantics but profiler still shows generic index_add/scatter
semantic_traps: Backward must return gradients for exactly the same inputs and None for non-differentiable inputs.
Saved tensor lifetime and device placement must match framework autograd expectations.
Recomputation can change numerical results if forward uses approximate math or random state.
Atomic gradient accumulation can be nondeterministic.
Training path requires stricter parity than eval-only fast path.
branch_generator_plan: start with model-local Python autograd wrapper and native fallback
capture forward/backward parity before writing HIP
specialize backward reduction when output domain is small or duplicate rate is high
fuse backward elementwise scale/bias/reduction when saved tensors are already available
keep env-controlled fallback until long-run accuracy is accepted
correctness_gates: torch.autograd.gradcheck when dtype and op permit
manual forward/backward parity against original implementation
small, real, and boundary shape tests
fallback path test with env off/on
short training smoke and project accuracy gate
stop_reasons: gradcheck or backward parity fails outside tolerance
saved tensor contract cannot be proven from project code
HIP branch is faster in isolation but training step or memory regresses
framework-level custom autograd wrapper already removes generic hotspot
operation participates in unsupported in-place or alias path
library_references: rocPRIM segmented reduction primitives for gradient accumulation

softmax_layernorm_row_reduction.scope: Row-wise softmax, layernorm, rmsnorm, masked row reductions, and fused row-wise epilogues.
profiler_symptoms: kernels or ops contain softmax, layernorm, rmsnorm, norm, row_reduce
separate max/sum/exp/divide or norm/mul/add kernels appear around one row operation
bandwidth-bound row reductions read the same row multiple times
hidden size or row width is stable across iterations
training path has separate backward norm/reduction hotspots
semantic_traps: Softmax must subtract max before exp for numerical stability.
Mask must be applied before normalization when reference semantics require it.
LayerNorm and RMSNorm are not interchangeable.
Backward may require saved mean/invstd or exact recomputation policy.
Tail columns and non-contiguous strides commonly break vectorized branches.
branch_generator_plan: one-row-per-block softmax or norm branch
one-wave-per-row branch for short rows
split-row branch for long rows with second-stage combine
fuse bias/mask/scale or residual only after semantic contract is captured
generate backward only when saved tensor contract is explicit
correctness_gates: masked rows and all-masked row if supported
row width not divisible by vector width
forward and backward parity when training is enabled
stop_reasons: row width is too small and launch overhead dominates
row width is too large and split overhead cancels gain
library/framework already fuses the operation
backward contract is incomplete
numerical tolerance fails on real-shape data
library_references: Triton fused softmax and layernorm tutorials as algorithmic patterns

matmul_gemm.scope: Dense, batched, grouped, sparse, quantized, or fused-epilogue matrix multiplication kernels.
profiler_symptoms: kernels or ops contain gemm, matmul, bmm, linear, moe, ck, blas, mmac, mfma
GEMM-like kernel has low achieved FLOPs
separate epilogue kernels for bias, activation, scale, quant/dequant, or layout conversion
many small GEMMs cause launch overhead
generated ISA lacks expected matrix-core instruction
semantic_traps: Do not replace a tuned BLAS or CK path with naive HIP.
Epilogue fusion must preserve beta, bias, scale, activation, and dtype rounding semantics.
Layout conversion cost must be included in e2e benchmark.
Quantized GEMM requires exact scale, zero-point, and saturation rules.
Generated source intent is not proof; check ISA.
branch_generator_plan: use rocBLAS/hipBLAS or CK Tile as first route for standard GEMM
generate tiled LDS HIP only as baseline or for custom fused shapes
try fused epilogue when output is single-use
bucket small/grouped GEMMs to reduce launch overhead
inspect dccobjdump for matrix instruction and resource usage
stop_reasons: library path already saturates expected throughput
custom kernel improves microbench but loses e2e
epilogue semantics incomplete
shape distribution too dynamic for specialization
generated ISA does not contain intended matrix instruction

topk_sort_selection.scope: Top-k, sorting, partial sorting, selection, routing, beam-search, and candidate filtering kernels.
profiler_symptoms: kernels or ops contain topk, sort, argsort, select, partial_sort, beam, sample, route, expert
multiple kernels implement compare, prefix, compact, and gather stages
CPU sync reads candidate counts or selected sizes
full sort appears when only K elements are needed
MoE or retrieval route dominated by selection plus dispatch
semantic_traps: Changing candidate set changes model semantics.
Tie ordering may affect downstream results.
Approximate selection is opt-in only.
NaN behavior must match framework reference.
Optimizing topk alone can regress dispatch or gather stages.
branch_generator_plan: replace full sort with partial sort or block top-k when exact top-k suffices
use per-wave or per-block register candidates for small K
use rocPRIM partial_sort/select/radix sort as baseline
fuse threshold/compact/gather only when output ordering contract is captured
profile whole routing pipeline for MoE/retrieval
stop_reasons: full ordering is semantically required
tie behavior cannot be matched
library primitive is faster or near bandwidth ceiling
selection is not a top share after pipeline profiling
optimized selection changes downstream distribution

required_contract_fields: whether layout is reused by multiple consumers
semantic_traps: Removing a copy can expose aliasing bugs.
Contiguous conversion may be required by downstream library.
Padding value and invalid-token zeroing are semantic, not cosmetic.
Layout change must include conversion cost in benchmark.
Async copies require correct synchronization before host/device reads.
branch_generator_plan: fuse transform with single-use producer or consumer
replace generic contiguous conversion with shape-specialized copy
vectorize aligned copy or pack
avoid transform entirely by changing consumer layout
batch small copies and remove redundant copies
correctness_gates: tail dimensions not divisible by vector width
stop_reasons: copy is required by external IO or library contract
layout is reused enough that fusion hurts another consumer
alignment/tail constraints prevent safe vectorization
benchmark gain disappears when full region is measured
host/device sync is the true bottleneck

AITER pack/unpack and cache layout patterns
